question: Who among the following was an ancient Indian mathematician-astronomer?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Varahamihira**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Varahamihira**, also known as Varaha or Mihira, **was an Indian philosopher, astronomer, and mathematician**. 
 
• He was born in** 505 A.D. in a Brahmin family at Kapittha, a village near Ujjain**.
 
• He **proposed that the Moon and planets are lustrous not because of their own light but due to sunlight**.
 
• He was one of the **nine gems of the court of **legendary ruler **Yashodharman Vikramaditya of Malwa**.
 
• Varahamihira’s main work is the book **Pancha Siddhantika **(Treatise on the five Astronomical Canons gives us information about older Indian texts which are now lost).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• His important works also include** Brahma Samhita** which covers wide-ranging subjects of human interest, including astrology, planetary movements, eclipses, rainfall, rainfall, clouds even domestic relations, gems, pearls, and rituals.
 
• Varahamihira’s mathematical work included** the discovery of trigonometric formulas**.
 
• He was inspired by the great mathematician and astrologer of India **Aryabhatta**.
 
 
• **Nagarjuna- Indian Buddhist Philosopher**
 
• **Banabhatta- Sanskrit prose writer and poet of India**
 
• **Amalananda- Sanskrit Scholar**
